Phase velocity tracks a surface of constant phase, whereas group velocity tracks the envelope of a wave packet. In a dispersive medium they can differ, so a rapidly moving phase pattern does not directly imply that information or energy travels at the same speed.

Inter-rater reliability measures how consistently different observers score the same material. High agreement does not prove the scoring rule measures the intended construct; raters can consistently apply a biased or irrelevant criterion.
Groundwater can precipitate minerals in sediment pore spaces and cement grains together during diagenesis. Cement strengthens rock but often reduces permeability by blocking connected flow paths.

Type Ia supernovae can be standardized using their light-curve properties and then used as luminous distance indicators. They are not intrinsically identical explosions, so modern distance work relies on empirical corrections rather than assuming perfect uniformity.

Lossless compression cannot make every possible message shorter on average without running out of distinct short codewords. Entropy sets a fundamental scale for average code length, so compression exploits unequal probabilities and structure rather than creating information capacity from nothing.

Time-series validation should respect temporal order so training data do not include information from the future relative to validation. Random shuffling can produce optimistic results when trends, seasonality, or delayed effects are present.

Beam search keeps several high-scoring partial sequences instead of only the best one at each step. A wider beam explores more candidates but does not guarantee more natural text because the model probability objective itself may favor short or repetitive sequences.

When p-type and n-type semiconductors contact, carriers diffuse and leave behind ionized dopants, creating a depletion region and built-in electric field. Equilibrium is reached when drift from the field balances further diffusion.

Stokes' theorem relates the flux of curl through a surface to circulation around its boundary. The orientation of the boundary must be consistent with the chosen surface normal; reversing orientation reverses the sign.

A checksum is usually designed to detect accidental transmission errors cheaply, while a cryptographic hash is designed to resist deliberate collision and preimage attacks. Both map data to compact values, but their threat models and guarantees differ.

Speculative execution performs work before it is certain that the work will be needed. Correctly designed hardware discards wrong-path architectural results, but microarchitectural side effects such as cache changes can still matter for security and performance.

Lock-in detection uses a known reference frequency to retain signal components coherent with that reference, allowing weak periodic signals to be extracted from strong broadband noise. It does not remove all noise; it narrows the effective measurement bandwidth.

Cavitation occurs when local liquid pressure falls low enough for vapor cavities to form. Their later collapse in higher-pressure regions can create noise, vibration, and surface damage, so the problem is controlled by local pressure rather than simply by average system pressure.

Two solids in contact can have a temperature jump at the interface because microscopic contact area and vibrational mismatch impede heat flow. Interface thermal resistance can dominate nanoscale systems even when both bulk materials are good conductors.

Calling one elementary step the rate-determining step can be a useful approximation, but real multistep kinetics may depend on several intermediates and pre-equilibria. The observed rate law should be derived from or tested against the mechanism rather than guessed from a diagram.

A promoter is a DNA region that helps position transcription machinery near a gene. Promoter strength is not an intrinsic universal number because activity depends on cell type, regulatory proteins, chromatin state, and surrounding sequence.

Two waves with nearby frequencies interfere to produce beats: rapid oscillations sit inside a slowly varying envelope. The beat rate is set by the frequency difference, so periodic loudness changes need not mean either source is modulating its own amplitude.

Ordinary generating functions naturally encode many unlabelled counting problems, while exponential generating functions divide coefficients by factorials and often match labelled structures. The choice reflects the combinatorial composition rules rather than a purely cosmetic convention.

Polarizing a dielectric slightly separates positive and negative charge within matter. The material can remain electrically neutral overall while bound charge appears on surfaces or wherever polarization varies spatially.

Hamiltonian phase-space flow preserves volume according to Liouville's theorem. A cloud of initial states may stretch and fold, but the dynamics cannot compress its total phase-space volume, unlike dissipative systems whose trajectories can contract toward attractors.

At thermal equilibrium, a good absorber at a given wavelength and direction is also a good emitter there. A shiny surface can therefore reduce both absorption and emission relative to a black surface under the same conditions.

Soft switching arranges circuit dynamics so a transistor turns on or off when voltage or current is near zero. It reduces switching loss and electromagnetic interference but may require extra circulating energy or components.

Raoult's law states that an ideal solution's component vapor pressure equals its liquid mole fraction times the pure-component vapor pressure. Positive or negative deviations reveal that unlike-molecule interactions differ from the idealized average.

Comoving coordinates factor out the average expansion of the universe so objects following the Hubble flow can keep nearly fixed comoving positions. Their proper separation can still grow with time as the cosmic scale factor increases.

Copy-on-write lets multiple mappings share a physical page until one side attempts to modify it. The expensive copy is deferred until needed, so rapidly creating a process does not imply that its entire memory image has already been duplicated.

An ideal is a subset of a ring closed under addition and absorption by multiplication from the ring. Ideals play the role that normal subgroups play in group theory because they are precisely the subsets that permit quotient rings.

Cellular respiration does not release all chemical energy from fuel in one step. A sequence of redox reactions builds an electrochemical gradient across a membrane, and ATP synthase uses that gradient to make ATP in a controlled energy-conversion process.

Normally temperature falls with height through much of the lower atmosphere, but an inversion has warmer air over cooler air. This configuration resists vertical mixing and can trap pollutants or fog near the surface.

A dissolved solute lowers the chemical potential of the solvent in the liquid phase, while the pure solid solvent follows a different temperature dependence. The new solid-liquid equilibrium therefore occurs at a lower temperature, providing a thermodynamic explanation of freezing-point depression.

Repeated loading can nucleate and grow cracks at stresses far below a material's one-time static fracture strength. Fatigue life therefore depends not only on the maximum load but also on stress amplitude, mean stress, notches, surface condition, and environment.

A permutation test builds a reference distribution by rearranging labels or assignments that are exchangeable under the null hypothesis. Its validity comes from the randomization symmetry, so arbitrary shuffling is invalid when observations have dependence or unequal assignment structure.

A fuel cell's open-circuit voltage is set by reaction thermodynamics, but under load activation, ohmic, and mass-transport losses reduce terminal voltage as current rises. Performance improvements therefore involve catalysis, conductivity, and reactant transport together.

After recrystallization, continued heating can drive larger grains to grow at the expense of smaller ones because reducing total grain-boundary area lowers energy. Excessive grain growth can reduce strength even though the material is becoming structurally more equilibrated.

Near a black hole there is an innermost stable circular orbit whose radius depends on black-hole spin and orbital direction. Inside it, stable circular motion is no longer possible, strongly influencing the inner structure and efficiency of accretion disks.

Sound waves once traveled through the photon-baryon plasma of the early universe and left a preferred comoving separation scale in later matter structure. That fossil scale acts as a standard ruler for expansion history; it is not an ongoing acoustic wave between present-day galaxies.

In a close binary, one star can expand until matter crosses an effective gravitational boundary and flows toward its companion. Binary evolution can therefore differ radically from isolated-star evolution even when the initial stellar masses are similar.

Electric potential is defined only up to an additive constant; measurable voltage depends on potential differences. Setting zero potential at infinity is convenient for isolated systems, but other reference choices are equally valid when used consistently.

Light carries momentum as well as energy, so absorption or reflection transfers mechanical momentum and produces radiation pressure. Ideal reflection transfers more normal momentum than absorption, which is the physical basis of photon-pressure propulsion such as light sails.

Random error produces scatter and can often be reduced in an average by repeated measurements. Systematic error shifts results consistently in one direction, so simply collecting more repetitions does not make it disappear.

Many properties of random graphs appear abruptly near characteristic edge probabilities. Below a threshold the property is unlikely, while above it the property becomes likely, revealing phase-transition-like behavior in discrete structures.

As sediments are buried, grain rearrangement and pressure can reduce pore space and expel fluids. Compaction changes thickness, porosity, and permeability, so the present thickness of a sedimentary layer can be much smaller than its original depositional thickness.

Thermodynamic equilibrium expressions use activity rather than bare concentration. In sufficiently dilute solutions activity is often approximated by concentration, but stronger interactions at higher ionic strength can make that approximation inaccurate.

Standing-wave ratio arises from interference between forward and reflected waves and is commonly used to assess transmission-line matching. A value near one indicates little reflection, but SWR alone does not reveal the location or exact nature of the mismatch.

A birefringent material presents different effective refractive indices to different polarizations, so components of one beam accumulate phase at different rates. Wave plates exploit this phase difference to transform polarization rather than simply absorbing one component.

Learning-rate warmup starts optimization with smaller steps and increases them gradually. It can stabilize training when early gradients, normalization statistics, or adaptive optimizer states are poorly calibrated, especially in large models.

Eukaryotic RNA transcripts can be capped, spliced, edited, and polyadenylated before functioning as mature RNA. Gene expression therefore involves substantial information processing after transcription rather than a one-step copy from DNA.

The Walker circulation is an east-west tropical atmospheric overturning linked to sea-surface temperature contrasts across the equatorial Pacific. Changes in this circulation interact with ocean upwelling and are central to El Niño-Southern Oscillation.

Pointwise convergence lets different inputs approach the limiting function at unrelated rates, while uniform convergence requires one error bound to work across the whole domain. That stronger control is why uniform convergence preserves properties such as continuity under suitable conditions.

The minimum Hamming distance of an error-correcting code determines how many symbol errors can be detected or corrected reliably. Larger distance generally requires more redundancy, so coding trades transmission efficiency for robustness rather than treating all redundancy as waste.

Carnot efficiency is the ideal upper bound for a heat engine operating between two fixed temperatures and depends only on absolute temperatures. Reaching it requires reversible, idealized processes, so real engines have additional losses and lower efficiency.

Long polymer chains can become topologically entangled even without permanent chemical crosslinks. Entanglements strongly slow large-scale chain motion and give melts or rubbers mechanical behavior very different from collections of short molecules.

Having derivatives of every order does not guarantee that a function equals its Taylor series. Analyticity requires a locally convergent power-series representation, so smoothness is strictly weaker in real analysis.

Chemical weathering depends on temperature, water availability, rock type, and fresh surface area and is often faster in warm wet climates. Silicate weathering also consumes carbon dioxide over long timescales, linking geology with climate feedbacks.

The Clausius-Clapeyron relation connects how vapor pressure changes with temperature to the enthalpy of phase change under simplifying assumptions. It explains why a plot of log vapor pressure versus inverse temperature can be approximately linear over limited ranges.

Simple rule-of-mixtures estimates can bound or approximate composite properties when load sharing is idealized. Fiber orientation, interfaces, porosity, and geometry can make real behavior depart substantially from a naive volume-weighted average.

A ceiling effect occurs when many observations pile up near the maximum measurable score, hiding real differences among high-performing cases. Increasing sample size does not recover information that the measurement scale never recorded.

The steady-state approximation assumes a reactive intermediate is produced and consumed at nearly equal rates, so its concentration changes slowly. This does not mean the whole system is at chemical equilibrium; reactants can still be converted to products at a net rate.

Language-model cross-entropy measures the negative log probability assigned to the actual next token. A few true tokens given extremely low probability can contribute large loss, so the metric captures more than simple top-one accuracy and penalizes overconfident misallocation of probability.

A metric space abstracts distance through a function satisfying positivity, symmetry, and the triangle inequality. Euclidean distance is only one choice; changing the metric on the same underlying set can change convergence, neighborhoods, and continuity.

An azeotrope has vapor and liquid compositions that become equal at a particular mixture composition, preventing simple distillation from crossing that point under fixed pressure. It arises from nonideal vapor-liquid equilibrium rather than from a new pure compound necessarily forming.

Conducting waveguides support discrete field modes set by transverse boundary conditions, and each mode has a cutoff frequency. Below cutoff the field decays rather than propagating normally along the guide, so a waveguide does not transmit arbitrarily low frequencies.

Aggregate analysis bounds the total cost of a whole operation sequence directly and divides by the number of operations. Unlike average-case analysis, it needs no probability distribution over inputs; the guarantee applies to every allowed sequence of that length.

Ocean surface waves can travel in groups whose envelope moves at a different speed from individual crests. A crest may appear near the back of a group, move forward, and fade while the group itself continues.

Plastic deformation can increase dislocation density in a metal, and interacting dislocations make further slip harder. This produces work hardening: strength rises while ductility often falls. Annealing can later reduce that stored deformation through recovery and recrystallization.

In the canonical ensemble, Helmholtz free energy is directly related to the logarithm of the partition function. This converts microscopic statistical weights into a thermodynamic potential whose derivatives yield macroscopic quantities such as entropy and pressure.

Average precision summarizes a precision-recall ranking curve and emphasizes performance on positive examples. Its baseline depends on positive prevalence, so values should be interpreted relative to the class balance of the evaluation set.

A scaling law describes how one quantity changes as another varies, often through a power relation over a specified regime. Extrapolating the same exponent far beyond the measured range can fail when new mechanisms or characteristic scales appear.

A pump can cavitate if local inlet pressure falls too close to vapor pressure. Net positive suction head expresses the pressure margin, and increasing downstream discharge pressure does not necessarily cure an inadequate suction condition.

The RC time constant is not a fixed time at which a capacitor becomes completely charged. It sets the scale of an exponential response: after one time constant about 63 percent of the final change has occurred, while exact convergence is asymptotic.

For a differentiable convex function, every tangent line lies below the graph, turning local derivative information into a global lower bound. This structure makes every local minimum global, a conclusion that does not hold for general nonconvex functions.

Entropy coding assigns shorter representations to more probable symbols and longer ones to less probable symbols. Its performance depends on how accurately the probability model matches the source; a poor model can squander compression even with an optimal coder.

A solubility product describes the equilibrium activity relation between a sparingly soluble solid and its ions. An ionic product above Ksp gives a thermodynamic drive to precipitate, yet nucleation barriers can permit supersaturation before visible crystals appear.

Mechanistic evidence explains how a cause could influence an outcome through intermediate processes and can strengthen causal interpretation. A plausible mechanism does not replace sound comparative design, because confounding can still make the proposed pathway secondary or misleading.

Snapshot isolation lets a transaction read from a consistent snapshot while preventing certain write-write conflicts. It avoids many anomalies but is weaker than full serializability and can permit write skew when transactions update different rows based on a shared condition.
Water and other volatiles can dissolve in magma more readily at high pressure. As magma rises and pressure falls, gases exsolve and expand, potentially driving fragmentation and explosive eruption.

Measurement traceability links a result to recognized reference standards through a documented unbroken chain of calibrations, each with stated uncertainty. It is not merely a label saying an instrument was calibrated; it establishes evidence for comparability.

Median absolute deviation measures spread using distances from the median and is robust to outliers. A scaling constant is often applied to make it comparable to standard deviation under a normal model, but the raw MAD has its own direct interpretation.

A solar cell's fill factor compares maximum electrical power with the product of open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current. Series resistance, leakage, and recombination all reduce the squareness of the current-voltage curve, so open-circuit voltage alone does not determine device quality.

Differential privacy bounds how much the output distribution of an analysis can change when one individual's record is added or removed. Privacy comes from a quantitative stability guarantee, usually requiring randomness, and repeated analyses consume a privacy budget.

Möbius inversion reverses certain sums taken over divisibility or more general partially ordered sets. It plays the role of an algebraic undoing operation, recovering local quantities from cumulative sums through alternating structure encoded by the Möbius function.

Radioactive half-life describes the statistical decay of a large population of nuclei. It does not mean every individual nucleus survives exactly half a lifetime; single decay times are unpredictable while aggregate decay follows a stable law.

If a viscoelastic material is held at fixed strain, the stress needed to maintain that deformation can decrease with time. Stress relaxation is distinct from creep, where stress is held approximately fixed and strain changes.

A digital signature uses a private key to create evidence that anyone with the public key can verify. It authenticates a message and detects modification but does not hide the message contents, so signatures and encryption solve different problems.

The same chemical composition can crystallize in more than one structure, a phenomenon called polymorphism. Different polymorphs can have different density, solubility, mechanical, or electronic properties, so composition alone does not fully determine a solid's behavior.

An inductor stores energy in its magnetic field when current flows. Self-inductance measures how strongly a circuit's own current links magnetic flux back through the circuit, making rapid current changes energetically costly.

Battery C-rate expresses current relative to rated capacity; 1C is roughly the current that would deliver the rated capacity in one hour under specified conditions. Higher C-rates increase polarization and heating and can reduce usable capacity, so they do more than simply rescale time.

Polarization describes how the electric-field vector changes orientation in time. Linear, circular, and elliptical polarization are not different kinds of light; they are different states of the same transverse wave degree of freedom.

A hotter blackbody emits more total power and shifts its spectral peak toward shorter wavelengths. The peak wavelength changes with temperature, but the spectrum remains broad; a blackbody does not emit only at one characteristic color.

Quantum field theory in curved spacetime predicts that black holes have a temperature inversely related to mass and can emit Hawking radiation. For astrophysical black holes the temperature is extremely low, so the effect is negligible compared with ordinary surrounding radiation today.

Batch normalization uses batch statistics during training but typically stored running statistics during evaluation. Very small or nonrepresentative batches can make training behavior noisy, and forgetting to switch modes can change predictions.

Storage engines can use Bloom filters to avoid unnecessary disk lookups for keys that are definitely absent. False positives still trigger some needless reads, but false negatives are avoided when the filter is implemented correctly.

Lenz's law says induced effects oppose the change in magnetic flux that produced them. This opposition is not purposeful behavior by the field; it is an expression of energy conservation, since reinforcing the original change would permit self-amplifying energy production.

An ideal boost converter can raise voltage by storing energy in an inductor and releasing it at a higher output potential. Higher voltage does not create extra power; current capability and losses must adjust so energy conservation still holds.

Absorbed light can create mobile charge carriers and increase a semiconductor's conductivity. The response depends on absorption, carrier lifetime, trapping, and mobility, so stronger illumination does not translate into identical conductivity changes in every material.

Marine organic matter often shows approximate recurring ratios among carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus, summarized by the Redfield ratio. It is a broad biogeochemical pattern rather than an exact composition that every organism or ocean region must obey.

Recombination during meiosis exchanges DNA segments between homologous chromosomes and creates new combinations of alleles. It does not generate all new mutations from nothing; it reshuffles existing variation and increases genetic combinations among offspring.

Electronegativity differences help predict bond polarity by indicating unequal electron sharing. Molecular polarity also depends on geometry, so a molecule can contain polar bonds yet have nearly zero net dipole if their vector contributions cancel.

Run-length encoding compresses long repeats by storing a value and count. It can expand data with frequent alternation, demonstrating that a compression method's usefulness depends on source structure rather than on the method being universally "efficient.".

London dispersion forces arise from correlated instantaneous fluctuations in electron clouds and occur between all atoms and molecules. They often grow with polarizability and contact area, so large nonpolar molecules can still attract one another strongly.

A shock wave compresses and heats a supersonic flow through a very thin region. Unlike a smooth reversible compression, a real shock increases entropy and destroys some mechanical availability even when total energy is conserved.

A Newtonian fluid has shear stress proportional to shear rate with a constant viscosity at fixed state. Many suspensions, polymers, and complex fluids violate this relation, so viscosity can depend on shear rate or deformation history.

A population bottleneck can randomly remove much genetic variation when population size collapses. Even if census numbers later recover, genetic diversity need not return automatically; mutation, migration, and time are needed to rebuild variation.

Internal validity concerns whether a causal comparison is credible within a study, while external validity concerns transfer to other populations, settings, or times. Tight experimental control can improve internal validity without automatically guaranteeing real-world generalization.

The median is less sensitive than the mean to a few extreme observations because only rank order matters. Robustness is not immunity: if more than half the data are contaminated, even the median can be moved arbitrarily far.

A concentration cell can generate voltage even when both electrodes use the same chemical couple because the activities differ. The cell converts free energy associated with concentration imbalance into electrical work as the system moves toward equilibrium.

The Poisson distribution models counts when many opportunities each have small event probability under suitable independence conditions. Its mean equals its variance, so data with strong overdispersion can signal clustering or heterogeneity beyond a simple Poisson model.

Inductor current and capacitor voltage in switching converters contain ripple because energy is moved in discrete switching intervals. Larger inductance, capacitance, or switching frequency can reduce ripple but increase size, cost, or switching loss.

Continued fractions represent real numbers through nested integer reciprocals. Their convergents give exceptionally good rational approximations, and periodic continued fractions characterize quadratic irrational numbers.

Consistent hashing maps keys and nodes into the same circular space so that adding or removing a node remaps mainly nearby keys rather than almost the entire dataset. Virtual nodes help smooth load because a few physical node positions may otherwise be uneven.

A power series has a radius of convergence: it converges absolutely inside the radius and diverges outside, while boundary points require separate analysis. Knowing the radius alone does not determine endpoint behavior.

Elastic deformation is recoverable when load is removed, whereas plastic deformation leaves permanent strain. The transition is governed by material mechanisms and stress state; it is not simply the point where a specimen first looks visibly bent.

An ideal buck converter produces an average output voltage related to input voltage by switch duty cycle in continuous conduction. Real output also depends on switching losses, resistance, control dynamics, and whether current becomes discontinuous.

A field extension enlarges a field by adding new elements while preserving field operations. Adjoining a root of an irreducible polynomial creates a finite-dimensional vector space over the original field, linking field theory with linear algebra.

During a planetary transit, the fractional loss of starlight is approximately the squared planet-to-star radius ratio in an ideal case. Starspots, grazing geometry, and stellar-radius uncertainty complicate the inference, so transit depth is not a perfectly direct ruler.

Broad X-ray diffraction peaks can result from small coherent crystallite size, lattice strain, instrument resolution, or overlapping phases. Using peak width as a direct grain-size meter without separating these contributions can be misleading.

Adding fins increases heat-transfer area, but a fin is not isothermal; temperature usually falls toward its tip. Fin efficiency compares actual heat transfer with the ideal case where the whole fin remains at base temperature.

Coupled oscillators can be decomposed into normal modes, collective patterns that evolve independently in the linear approximation. Each normal mode has its own frequency, and arbitrary small motions can be built as superpositions of these modes.

When the chance of missingness depends on the unseen value even after conditioning on observed information, the process is missing not at random. The missingness mechanism then cannot generally be identified from observed data alone without additional assumptions.

Processors often predict function returns with a small return-address stack rather than a generic branch predictor. Nested calls naturally push and pop return locations, while unusual control flow or deep nesting can overflow the structure and reduce prediction accuracy.

Bootstrap confidence intervals use the empirical sample to approximate repeated sampling of an estimator. Different constructions such as percentile and bias-corrected intervals make different approximations, and all can struggle when the original sample poorly represents the target population.

Geothermal gradient describes how temperature increases with depth, but it is not globally constant. Tectonics, heat flow, thermal conductivity, and groundwater alter local gradients, so shallow measurements cannot be linearly extrapolated to Earth's core.

At a eutectic point, a liquid of one specific composition transforms into two solid phases at the lowest melting temperature of that binary system. Off-eutectic alloys usually precipitate a primary phase first before the remaining liquid approaches eutectic composition.

Geometrically, at a constrained extremum the objective gradient cannot have a component along feasible tangent directions, so it must lie in the normal space spanned by constraint gradients. The Lagrange multiplier is a consequence of that geometry, not an arbitrary extra variable.

A Diophantine equation asks for integer or rational solutions rather than arbitrary real solutions. A polynomial equation may be easy over the reals yet difficult over the integers because divisibility and modular constraints introduce discrete structure.

Transform faults accommodate mainly horizontal plate motion without creating or destroying large amounts of lithosphere. They can still accumulate elastic strain and produce major earthquakes, so subduction is not required for strong seismic hazard.

Byte-level tokenization can represent arbitrary text without unknown characters because every input reduces to bytes. The cost is that some scripts or unusual strings may require many tokens, increasing effective sequence length.

Energy conservation tracks quantity, while exergy tracks how much useful work could ideally be obtained relative to an environment. Equal amounts of heat at very different temperatures can carry the same energy but different exergy.

Content-defined chunking chooses data boundaries from the data pattern itself rather than fixed byte offsets. Inserting bytes near the beginning then shifts only nearby chunks instead of all later boundaries, improving deduplication of edited files.

Teacher forcing supplies true previous tokens during training, whereas autoregressive generation must condition on its own past outputs. This mismatch can make errors compound during generation, a phenomenon often called exposure bias.

Aerodynamic lift can be described through pressure differences associated with circulation around an airfoil. The explanation is compatible with momentum deflection of the air; these are not competing laws but different views of the same force balance.

A quotient group treats elements that differ by a normal subgroup as belonging to the same coset. Normality is essential because it makes multiplication of cosets well defined; an arbitrary subgroup does not generally produce a quotient group.

Graph coloring assigns colors so adjacent vertices differ. The chromatic number depends on global graph structure rather than just maximum degree, and deciding the minimum coloring for a general graph is computationally difficult.

Extreme observations often move closer to the population average on repeat measurement because the first extreme value contains random fluctuation. Selecting only extreme cases before an intervention can therefore make ordinary regression to the mean look like a treatment effect.

Whether an RLC system oscillates depends on the competition between energy storage and damping. Underdamping gives decaying oscillations, critical damping gives the fastest nonoscillatory return, and excessive damping can make the return to equilibrium slower.

A strain gauge changes resistance with mechanical strain, with sensitivity described by the gauge factor. Resistance change does not automatically represent strain alone because temperature also affects resistance, so practical systems often use compensation.

In a DC motor with approximately fixed magnetic flux, torque is roughly proportional to armature current. Speed is influenced by voltage and back emf, so current and speed should not be treated as interchangeable measures of motor output.

A circular aperture images a point source as an Airy pattern with a central disk and diffraction rings. The disk scale depends on wavelength and aperture, so resolving two points is controlled by the optical point-spread function rather than detector pixel spacing alone.

A phonon is a quantized collective excitation of a crystal's normal modes, not a tiny literal particle sitting between atoms. The phonon description organizes lattice heat capacity, thermal transport, and electron-lattice scattering within one framework.

A high learning rate can accelerate early progress while a lower rate later helps settle into a good region. Schedules exploit this changing optimization need, so one constant learning rate may be unnecessarily conservative or unstable across the entire run.

The s-process builds heavy nuclei through neutron captures slow enough that unstable nuclei usually beta-decay before capturing another neutron. It operates in environments such as evolved stars and follows a path relatively close to stable isotopes.

A caldera can form when a large eruption or magma withdrawal leaves insufficient support for the overlying rock and the surface collapses. It is not simply an unusually large crater excavated only by explosive force.

Momentum accumulates a velocity-like running direction from past gradients, reducing zigzag motion in narrow valleys and preserving progress along consistent directions. Too much momentum can overshoot or amplify instability when the objective changes sharply.

A binomial distribution with many trials and small success probability approaches a Poisson distribution when the expected count stays fixed. The approximation concerns a particular scaling limit, not every large-n binomial situation.

A color-magnitude diagram plots observed stellar color against brightness for a population such as a cluster. Unlike a theoretical luminosity-temperature diagram, it works directly with measured passbands and must account for distance and extinction when comparing different populations.
An ideal gear pair trades angular speed for torque while conserving power apart from losses. A higher output torque from reduction gearing does not create energy; output speed falls correspondingly.

A magnetic core has a finite range over which flux density grows approximately proportionally with magnetizing field. Near saturation, inductance falls and magnetizing current can rise sharply, so applying too much voltage at too low a frequency can overheat a transformer.

A write-back cache updates main memory only when a modified cache line is evicted, reducing memory traffic. The cache must track dirty lines, and data can temporarily exist only in the cache until explicit or automatic writeback occurs.

The exponential distribution is the continuous memoryless waiting-time distribution. Its constant hazard rate means that survival up to the present does not change the instantaneous event rate, a property that is often unrealistic for aging components.

A distributed snapshot aims to record a state that could have existed consistently across processes despite messages in flight. The challenge is not reading every node at the same physical instant but preserving a causally valid cut through distributed events.
A molecular dipole moment is a vector sum of charge separation throughout the molecule. Changing molecular geometry can therefore change polarity even when the individual bond types remain the same.

Active transport moves substances against an electrochemical gradient by coupling transport to another energy source such as ATP hydrolysis or a second ion gradient. The transported molecule does not violate diffusion; external free energy changes the combined process.

Vorticity measures local rotational tendency in a fluid and is related to the curl of velocity. A curved streamline does not automatically imply large local vorticity, and a fluid element can move along a curved path without spinning strongly about its own center.

The potential method in amortized analysis assigns stored credit to a data structure's state. A cheap operation may increase potential and prepay future work, while an expensive operation can draw down that stored potential.

A brown dwarf forms like a star but has too little mass to sustain ordinary hydrogen fusion in its core. Some can briefly burn deuterium, so the boundary between giant planets and low-mass stars depends on formation and nuclear criteria rather than brightness alone.

The actual tidal range of a coastline depends strongly on basin shape and resonant response, not only on astronomical forcing. A bay whose natural oscillation period aligns with tidal forcing can amplify water-level changes dramatically.

Wind-driven ocean motion is deflected by Earth's rotation, and the vertically integrated Ekman transport is roughly perpendicular to the wind in an idealized setting. Divergence of this transport can pull deeper water upward and create coastal upwelling.

At high temperature, a material under constant stress below its room-temperature yield strength can still accumulate permanent strain over time through creep. The balance among dislocation climb, diffusion, and grain-boundary processes depends on temperature, stress, and grain size.

Niche partitioning allows similar species to coexist by using different resources, times, or microhabitats and thereby reducing direct competition. Sharing the same geographic area does not mean two species use the environment in identical ways.

Poisson's ratio relates transverse strain to axial strain during uniaxial loading. Most common solids become narrower when stretched, but some engineered and natural auxetic structures can expand laterally and have a negative effective Poisson ratio.

In an undeformed sedimentary sequence, younger layers generally lie above older layers. Folding, faulting, intrusion, or overturned beds can disturb that simple ordering, so geological context must be checked before applying superposition mechanically.

In a direct-gap semiconductor, the conduction-band minimum and valence-band maximum occur at nearly the same crystal momentum, making radiative recombination efficient. An indirect-gap material often needs a phonon to conserve momentum, which is one reason silicon emits light poorly.

Past ice sheets depressed Earth's crust and altered mantle flow. Thousands of years after melting, the land and gravitational field continue to readjust, affecting modern measurements of sea level and crustal motion.

For a fixed transmitted real power, raising voltage reduces current and therefore resistive I-squared-R losses. High-voltage transmission trades lower conductor loss against insulation, clearance, equipment, and safety requirements.

The inverse function theorem uses a nonsingular Jacobian to guarantee a smooth local inverse near a point. A nonzero Jacobian determinant is a local condition and does not by itself prove global one-to-one behavior.

A database checkpoint records progress that limits how far recovery must scan through the log. It does not mean every transaction is finished or every page is perfectly synchronized at one instant; modern checkpoints can proceed while the database remains active.

Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation samples plausible input values from their joint uncertainty distribution and repeatedly evaluates the model. It handles nonlinear transformations and asymmetric outputs naturally, provided the assumed input distributions and correlations are credible.

Maximum-entropy reasoning chooses the distribution that adds the least extra structure beyond stated constraints. For a continuous variable with fixed mean and variance, the Gaussian has maximum entropy; this is an information principle, not a claim of maximal physical disorder.

Crystalline materials produce sharp diffraction peaks because periodic planes reinforce scattering at specific conditions. Amorphous materials instead tend to show broad diffuse features, reflecting short-range order without long-range periodic repetition.

In a linear medium, overlapping waves add without permanently changing one another. Interference can create large or nearly zero instantaneous amplitude, but after crossing, ideal linear waves continue with their original forms.

Covariate shift describes a setting where the input distribution changes while the conditional relationship between labels and inputs is assumed stable. Reweighting can sometimes correct evaluation or training, but only if the unchanged-conditional assumption is plausible.

A competitive inhibitor reduces substrate access to the active site and its effect can often be partly overcome by increasing substrate concentration. In the simplest kinetic model, apparent affinity changes while the maximum rate at saturating substrate remains unchanged.

A signal localized sharply in time generally requires a broad frequency spectrum, while resolving a very narrow frequency component requires observation over a longer time. This time-frequency tradeoff follows from Fourier structure rather than merely from imperfect instruments.

A zero-knowledge proof can convince a verifier that a statement is true without revealing the underlying secret beyond what the statement itself implies. The concept concerns information leakage from the proof transcript, not a guarantee that the surrounding system reveals nothing.

A planetary nebula forms when a low- or intermediate-mass star sheds outer layers late in life and a hot remnant ionizes the expanding gas. The name is historical; the object has nothing to do with planet formation.

Mini-batch gradients fluctuate around the full-data gradient. Smaller batches produce noisier updates that can aid exploration but reduce hardware efficiency, while very large batches give smoother estimates yet can require different learning-rate and regularization choices.

Hydrogen bonds are not merely strong generic dipole attractions. Their strength depends on donor-acceptor chemistry and geometry, making them relatively directional and important in organizing molecular structures.

Distillation separates components because vapor is enriched in the more volatile species relative to the liquid. Separation becomes difficult when relative volatility approaches one, regardless of how many times the mixture is simply boiled without staged contact.

Henry's law relates dissolved gas concentration to gas partial pressure in sufficiently dilute conditions. The proportionality depends on gas, solvent, and temperature, and it can fail when the gas reacts strongly with the solvent or the solution is nonideal.

During a first-order phase transition, energy can be absorbed or released without an immediate temperature change because it changes molecular organization rather than average thermal motion. Latent heat is therefore not evidence that energy transfer has stopped.

Heat-exchanger effectiveness compares actual heat transfer with the maximum thermodynamically possible transfer for the inlet conditions. A physically larger exchanger can increase effectiveness, but diminishing temperature differences prevent heat transfer from growing without bound.

In a star cluster whose members formed at roughly the same time, the mass of stars just leaving the main sequence provides an age indicator. Massive stars evolve faster, so an older cluster has a lower-mass main-sequence turnoff.

Particles much smaller than visible wavelengths scatter shorter wavelengths more strongly, approximately with an inverse fourth-power dependence under Rayleigh conditions. This helps explain the blue daytime sky, while sunsets involve long paths that remove much of the short-wavelength light.

A laser reaches threshold when round-trip optical gain balances cavity and output losses. Above threshold, additional pump power mainly increases coherent output while gain tends to be clamped near the value required to compensate losses.

General relativity predicts gravitational waves with transverse tidal distortions that stretch one spatial direction while squeezing the perpendicular direction. Interferometers measure tiny differential changes in arm lengths rather than detecting a force pushing the entire instrument one way.

Battery internal resistance causes terminal-voltage drop and heat generation under load. It is not a single ideal resistor constant across frequency, temperature, and state of charge; electrochemical polarization and diffusion add dynamic behavior.

The ordinary bootstrap resamples observations with replacement to mimic variability under an iid sampling picture. Strong temporal or spatial dependence breaks that picture, so block or other structured resampling methods may be needed to preserve dependence.

Lattice thermal conductivity depends on how far phonons travel before scattering from other phonons, defects, boundaries, or electrons. Adding defects can lower thermal conductivity even when the crystal remains mechanically intact.

Compressing a gas raises its temperature as work is added. Multistage compression with intercooling can reduce required work by removing heat between stages, showing why the path of compression matters even between similar inlet and outlet pressures.

Convective heat transfer depends strongly on the thin fluid region near a surface where velocity and temperature adjust to boundary conditions. Turbulence can thin or mix this boundary layer and often increases heat transfer.

Galois theory studies field automorphisms that preserve a base field and relates their symmetry group to intermediate fields. It explains why solvability of polynomial equations by radicals is controlled by algebraic symmetry rather than by clever formula manipulation alone.

Delta encoding stores differences between nearby values instead of absolute values. It is effective when consecutive values change slowly, and it often works best as a preprocessing step before another entropy coder.

A liquid can cool below its equilibrium freezing temperature without crystallizing when nucleation is delayed. The state is metastable rather than truly equilibrium liquid, and a disturbance or seed crystal can trigger rapid freezing.

Ionic strength weights ion concentration by the square of charge, so a small amount of a multivalent ion can influence solution electrostatics strongly. It helps explain why activity coefficients depend on the whole ionic environment rather than only on one species' concentration.

The total radiated power per unit area of an ideal blackbody scales as the fourth power of absolute temperature. Because the dependence is so steep, doubling temperature produces far more than twice the radiated flux.

In wind-driven ocean circulation, variation of the Coriolis parameter with latitude causes return flow to concentrate in strong western boundary currents. This dynamical asymmetry helps explain currents such as the Gulf Stream and Kuroshio.

Statistical significance depends on effect size, sample size, and noise, so a huge dataset can make a tiny difference highly significant. Effect size addresses magnitude, while a p-value addresses compatibility with a null model; the two answer different questions.

Cepheid variables follow a relation between pulsation period and intrinsic luminosity. Measuring the period helps infer true brightness and hence distance from the apparent brightness, though calibration and factors such as metallicity matter for precision.

A prism separates colors because refractive index generally varies with wavelength. The bending difference is caused by material dispersion rather than by different colors experiencing different geometric angles at the same refractive index.

Some metals are thermodynamically prone to oxidation yet form dense, adherent surface films that greatly slow further corrosion. Passivation shows why a favorable oxidation reaction does not automatically imply a high long-term corrosion rate.

An Eulerian cycle uses every edge exactly once, whereas a Hamiltonian cycle visits every vertex exactly once. Similar wording hides very different structures: Eulerian existence has a simple degree characterization, while Hamiltonian existence is generally much harder.

Distributed machines cannot keep perfectly identical physical clocks because oscillators drift and network delays are variable. Synchronization protocols estimate offsets within uncertainty bounds, so timestamps from different hosts should not automatically be treated as exact global order.

Reducing grain size often raises the yield strength of polycrystalline metals because more grain boundaries impede long-range dislocation motion. The Hall-Petch trend has a range of validity; at extremely small nanocrystalline sizes, other deformation mechanisms can become important.

Small nonpolar molecules can often cross lipid bilayers by passive diffusion, whereas ions face a large energetic barrier in the hydrophobic membrane core. Ion channels solve this by providing selective hydrophilic pathways rather than by making the entire membrane permeable.

A cell membrane is not a static lipid wall; many lipids and proteins move laterally within it. Fatty-acid saturation, chain length, and sterol content alter fluidity, helping membranes balance stability with flexibility across temperatures.

Marine productivity can be limited by different nutrients in different regions. Adding more of a nonlimiting nutrient may have little effect, so identifying the limiting resource requires understanding local supply, biological demand, and chemical availability.

A common-envelope phase can occur when one star engulfs its companion and both orbit inside a shared gaseous envelope. Drag extracts orbital energy and angular momentum, potentially ejecting the envelope and leaving a much tighter binary.

For standard dense self-attention, memory and pairwise attention computation grow roughly quadratically with sequence length. Doubling context can therefore cost much more than doubling token count in a purely linear operation.

A freely corroding metal settles near a mixed potential where total anodic and cathodic currents balance. The net external current can be zero while substantial local oxidation and reduction continue, so zero measured current does not mean no corrosion.

A covering index contains all fields needed for a query, allowing the engine to answer without fetching base-table rows in favorable cases. The faster read path comes at the cost of a larger index and more work on writes.

Kullback-Leibler divergence measures information loss when one probability distribution is used in place of another, but it is not an ordinary distance: reversing the two distributions generally changes the value. The chosen direction can therefore alter optimization behavior.

Displacement current is not a stream of charges crossing an insulator. It is the magnetic effect associated with a time-varying electric field, and it restores current continuity in situations such as the gap between capacitor plates.

Much of a ferromagnet's response to modest fields can come from domain-wall motion rather than uniform rotation of every atomic moment. Defects can pin domain walls, so microstructure strongly influences coercivity and magnetic softness.

As the early universe cooled enough for electrons to remain bound to nuclei, the free-electron density fell sharply and photons stopped scattering so frequently, making the universe transparent. The historical term "recombination" does not mean atoms had literally formed once before.

A photovoltaic module's maximum-power operating point shifts with irradiance and temperature, so power electronics track an appropriate voltage dynamically. Holding the module at one fixed laboratory-optimal voltage wastes energy as conditions change.

A repetition penalty changes decoding preferences to reduce reuse of recent tokens or phrases. It can suppress loops, but excessive penalties may also discourage legitimate recurrence such as names, technical terms, or syntactic agreement.

An absorbing state cannot be left once entered. In an absorbing Markov chain, expected absorption times and probabilities can be computed from transient-state dynamics, but absorption is not guaranteed unless the chain's structure makes every transient state eventually reach an absorber.

A Bayes factor compares how well two statistical models predict the observed data after averaging over their parameter priors. It is evidence from the data, not posterior probability by itself; posterior odds also include prior model odds.

Caches work because programs often reuse recently accessed data and access nearby addresses. Temporal and spatial locality are statistical tendencies rather than guarantees, so workloads with random large-memory access can defeat otherwise fast cache hierarchies.
Groundwater flows from higher hydraulic head toward lower head, driven by hydraulic gradient rather than elevation alone. Pressure in a confined aquifer can even drive water upward in a well.

The grand canonical ensemble describes a system that can exchange both energy and particles with a reservoir, using temperature, volume, and chemical potential as control variables. Particle number then fluctuates around an average rather than remaining fixed as in the canonical ensemble.

Bragg's law relates diffraction angle, wavelength, and lattice-plane spacing when waves scattered from successive planes interfere constructively. A diffraction peak identifies spacing information, but interpreting full crystal structure requires intensities, symmetry, and multiple reflections.

AdamW applies weight decay separately from the adaptive gradient update. This decoupling makes the regularization effect more predictable than adding an L2 penalty inside Adam's rescaled gradient calculation.

Interrupts let a device request attention when work arrives, avoiding constant checking during idle periods. Polling can be more efficient at very high event rates because repeated interrupt overhead may exceed the cost of checking a device in a tight loop.

Several codons can encode the same amino acid, making the genetic code degenerate. Degeneracy reduces the effect of some nucleotide changes on protein sequence, but synonymous substitutions can still influence expression, RNA structure, or translation speed.

A posterior predictive distribution averages predictions over uncertainty in model parameters rather than plugging in only one best estimate. It therefore propagates parameter uncertainty into future observations, though it still inherits assumptions of the model class.

A negative absolute temperature in statistical mechanics is not colder than zero kelvin. It can occur only in special systems with an upper energy bound and inverted populations; in terms of spontaneous energy flow, such a state is effectively hotter than any positive temperature.

Power factor measures how much apparent AC power becomes average real power. Reactive loads can increase current without proportionally increasing useful work, so power-factor correction can reduce current and distribution losses even when real power demand is unchanged.

A cryptographic nonce is a value intended to be used once or remain unpredictable under a protocol's requirements. Reusing a nonce can be harmless in some schemes and catastrophic in others, so its security meaning depends on the construction.

A gas cloud can collapse gravitationally when self-gravity overwhelms pressure support on a sufficiently large mass or scale. Higher temperature raises the characteristic Jeans support, while greater density generally makes collapse easier.

Bernoulli's relation follows mechanical-energy conservation along a streamline for an idealized steady, incompressible, low-viscosity flow. Applying it across pumps, strong losses, or unrelated streamlines without accounting for added or dissipated energy can give wrong results.

Log loss strongly penalizes assigning extremely small probability to an outcome that actually occurs. This makes it sensitive to overconfident errors and useful when the quality of an entire predictive distribution matters.

Federated learning trains across decentralized data by moving model updates or optimization information instead of collecting all raw data centrally. This reduces one form of data movement but does not automatically provide privacy, because updates themselves can leak information.

Feedforward control anticipates measured disturbances or command changes and applies compensation before output error develops. It can respond quickly but depends strongly on model accuracy and disturbance measurement, so practical systems often combine feedforward with feedback.

Transfer RNA links nucleotide codons to amino acids during translation. Each tRNA is charged by an aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase, so accurate translation depends not only on codon-anticodon pairing but also on correct amino-acid attachment.

A ferromagnet's magnetization depends not only on the present field but also on its history, producing a hysteresis loop. The loop area represents energy lost per cycle, which is why transformer materials are chosen for both favorable permeability and low hysteretic loss.

Thermal fluctuations and dissipative response are not unrelated phenomena. Near equilibrium, fluctuation-dissipation relations connect spontaneous equilibrium fluctuations with how strongly the system responds to and dissipates small external perturbations.

Multilevel page tables avoid allocating one enormous flat translation table for an entire virtual address space. Lower-level tables can be created only for populated address regions, trading extra lookup steps for much lower memory overhead.

An intrinsic semiconductor generates electron-hole pairs thermally, so carrier concentration rises strongly with temperature. This behavior differs from an ordinary metal, whose carrier density is comparatively fixed while scattering usually dominates the temperature dependence of resistance.

Rossby number compares inertial motion with Coriolis effects. Small values indicate rotation strongly constrains the flow, while large values mean local inertia dominates, helping distinguish planetary-scale circulation from small laboratory-scale motion.

A white dwarf has no long-term central fusion source and gradually radiates stored thermal energy. Cooling becomes a cosmic clock: older white dwarfs are generally cooler, though crystallization and envelope physics influence the cooling rate.

Chebyshev's inequality can be obtained by applying Markov's inequality to squared deviation from the mean. It controls tail probability using only mean and variance and assumes no normal distribution, which gives broad validity at the price of a potentially loose bound.

Training data update model parameters, validation data guide model selection, and test data estimate final generalization after choices are frozen. Repeatedly choosing models based on test performance turns the test set into part of development and weakens its independence.

Heating a fluid from below can destabilize a purely conducting state when buoyancy overcomes viscous and thermal diffusion. Above a threshold, organized convection cells appear, illustrating how a smooth parameter change can trigger spontaneous pattern formation.

A context switch costs more than saving a few registers. It can disrupt caches, TLB state, branch predictors, and scheduling locality, so excessive fine-grained switching can reduce throughput even if each task does little work.

In a mixture, the contribution of one component to an extensive property can depend on composition. Partial molar quantities capture the infinitesimal change caused by adding that component, so they need not equal the pure substance's molar value.

Cooperative binding occurs when binding at one site changes affinity at another. Positive cooperativity creates a steeper response to concentration than independent sites would, allowing molecular systems to behave more like switches without being perfectly all-or-none.

The negative binomial distribution can describe the number of trials or failures required to reach a fixed number of successes, depending on convention. It also provides a flexible count model with variance larger than the mean in many parameterizations.

Because the universe has finite age and an evolving expansion rate, there are limits to what regions can have communicated with us. Different horizon definitions answer different causal questions, so "edge of the observable universe" is not a material boundary in space.

A slender member under compression can buckle laterally long before its material reaches yield stress. Critical load depends strongly on length, section stiffness, and end constraints, so a material-strength check alone can greatly overestimate capacity.

Cosmological redshift mainly reflects the stretching of light wavelengths as the universe expands and is not simply ordinary Doppler shift. At small redshift the numerical descriptions can resemble each other, while large redshift requires a cosmological model.

The memoryless structure of a Poisson process is reflected in independent stationary increments and exponential interarrival times. Having already waited a long time does not by itself make an event more likely in the next small interval.

Heating a cold-worked metal can nucleate and grow new low-dislocation grains, dramatically reducing stored deformation and hardness. Recrystallization temperature is not a fixed material constant; prior strain, purity, time, and grain size matter.

Hensel lifting extends a solution of a polynomial congruence modulo a prime to solutions modulo higher prime powers under suitable derivative conditions. It is a p-adic analogue of refining an approximate root rather than solving each modulus from scratch.

A keystone species need not be abundant; it can have a disproportionately large effect on community structure through food-web or habitat interactions. Keystone status is defined by ecological consequences, not simply by which species has the most biomass.

A supercritical fluid lies above its critical temperature and pressure and combines gas-like transport with liquid-like density over tunable conditions. Calling it simply a "gas under pressure" misses the absence of a liquid-vapor phase boundary in that region.

Sampling temperature rescales logits before softmax. Lower temperature concentrates probability on already-favored tokens, while higher temperature flattens the distribution; it changes generation randomness without modifying the trained model parameters.

A maximal proper ideal cannot be enlarged without becoming the whole ring. In a commutative ring with identity, quotienting by a maximal ideal produces a field, which is stronger than merely producing an integral domain.

A statistical model can be optimized perfectly yet remain misleading if its functional form, error structure, or variable relationships are misspecified. Finding the best parameters inside a model does not prove that the model adequately represents the data-generating process.

Transformer losses include winding resistance, magnetic hysteresis, eddy currents, stray fields, and auxiliary consumption. High efficiency at rated load does not imply zero no-load loss, because magnetizing the core itself consumes energy.

Path connectedness requires a continuous path between every pair of points and therefore implies connectedness. The converse fails in general, showing that being globally inseparable is weaker than being able to travel continuously between arbitrary points.

Some regularization penalties correspond mathematically to particular prior distributions under a maximum-a-posteriori interpretation. This connection can clarify why L2 and L1 penalties shrink parameters differently, while not making every use of regularization fully Bayesian.

Slightly acidic groundwater can dissolve carbonate rock along fractures, enlarging them into conduits, caves, and sinkholes. Karst groundwater can move rapidly through these openings, violating assumptions of slow flow through uniform porous media.

At low substrate concentration, adding substrate can strongly increase enzyme reaction rate. Once most active sites are occupied, the rate approaches a maximum and further substrate produces diminishing change, so reaction rate is not proportional to substrate indefinitely.

Bose-Einstein condensation is a macroscopic occupation of a quantum state, not simply a substance becoming cold and solid. Interactions, trapping geometry, dimensionality, and particle conservation affect how the phenomenon appears in real systems.

Even apparently touching conductors make real electrical contact only at microscopic asperities, producing contact resistance. Oxide films, pressure, and roughness affect it, and local heating at high current can further degrade the connection.

Surface tension makes curved interfaces sustain a pressure difference described by the Young-Laplace relation. Smaller droplets require larger internal overpressure, which is why curvature matters in bubbles and capillary phenomena.

Storm surge is an abnormal rise in coastal water level driven mainly by wind stress and low atmospheric pressure during storms. Its severity depends on storm track, shelf depth, coastline shape, tide timing, and waves rather than wind speed alone.

The first isomorphism theorem says that a homomorphism factors through the quotient by its kernel, producing an isomorphism between that quotient and the image. It formalizes the idea that the only information lost is what the kernel identifies.

Oceanic crust generally becomes older with distance from mid-ocean ridges, yet even the oldest surviving seafloor is much younger than many continental rocks because oceanic lithosphere is continually recycled at subduction zones.

Arithmetic coding represents an entire message as a subinterval whose size reflects the product of symbol probabilities. Unlike one-codeword-per-symbol methods, it can approach fractional-bit average rates over long sequences when the probability model is accurate.

Thermoelectric figure of merit combines Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity, temperature, and thermal conductivity. Raising one favorable property can worsen another, making materials optimization a coupled problem rather than a search for the highest conductivity alone.

A martingale has the property that, given the current information, the conditional expectation of the next value equals the present one. The fair-game analogy concerns conditional expectation, not the shape of individual paths, which can still wander upward or downward for long periods.

The near field of an antenna contains substantial stored energy and complicated spatial structure. Far enough away, the field approaches a radiation-dominated far-field regime, so distance laws from one region should not be applied blindly to the other.

A rising unsaturated air parcel cools mainly because decreasing pressure lets it expand and do work. Once condensation begins, latent heat release reduces the cooling rate, so dry and moist adiabatic lapse rates differ.

Gravitational microlensing usually does not resolve separate images; instead, a background star temporarily brightens as alignment changes. Because the signal is geometric, the method can reveal compact objects or planets that emit little light themselves.

A pump operating point is set by the intersection of the pump's pressure-flow characteristic and the piping system's required head curve. Changing a valve or pipe resistance moves the operating point even when the pump itself is unchanged.

A process tends to access a changing working set of pages over time. If available memory cannot hold the active working set, frequent page faults can cause thrashing, where the system spends more time moving pages than doing useful computation.

For a small cylindrical wire or pipe, adding a thin insulation layer can initially increase heat loss because surface area grows faster than conduction resistance. Beyond a critical radius, further insulation reduces loss in the usual way.

Counterflow heat exchangers maintain useful temperature differences over more of their length than equivalent parallel-flow designs. Under suitable conditions, the cold outlet can even become warmer than the hot outlet temperature at the opposite end, without violating local heat-flow direction.

A Wheatstone bridge detects small resistance changes by comparing two divider branches near balance. The differential output can be highly sensitive, which is useful for strain gauges and also allows arrangements that cancel common temperature drift.

Dimensional consistency is a necessary check on physical equations: terms added together must have compatible dimensions. Passing a unit check does not prove an equation is correct, but failing it reveals an error immediately.

Cold molecular clouds can fragment because molecules and dust radiate away thermal energy, preventing pressure from rising too rapidly during compression. Cooling therefore plays a central role in allowing gravity to create dense star-forming structures.

Vector clocks use per-node logical counters to represent causal relationships among distributed events. Incomparable vectors can indicate concurrency, so the mechanism captures partial causal order without automatically imposing one unique total order on all events.

Sea level can rise without adding water mass if seawater warms and expands, a steric effect. Melting floating sea ice has a much smaller direct effect on mean sea level than melting land ice because floating ice already displaces water.

A Brønsted acid donates a proton and a base accepts one, so loss of a proton converts an acid into its conjugate base. Acid and base strengths are linked: a strong acid generally has a weak conjugate base because of the underlying proton-transfer equilibrium.

In a prefix-free code, no codeword is the prefix of another, allowing symbols to be decoded sequentially without separators. Huffman coding exploits this structure to obtain an optimal symbol code for a specified probability model, not for every possible source model.

Frequentist confidence refers to the long-run coverage of the interval-producing procedure, not a posterior probability that one already-computed interval contains a fixed parameter. The distinction lies between the random sampling procedure and the fixed parameter.

A Bayesian credible interval contains a specified amount of posterior probability under the chosen model and prior. Its interpretation is conditional on those assumptions and differs from the repeated-sampling coverage definition of a frequentist confidence interval.

Group commit batches several transactions so one durable storage flush can confirm them together. This improves throughput by amortizing expensive synchronization, at the cost of a small waiting interval and more coupling among transaction completion times.

An index fossil is useful for correlating rock layers when the organism was geographically widespread but existed for a relatively short geological interval. Rarity or impressive size alone does not make a fossil a good time marker.

Some materials become much less fracture-tough as temperature falls because plastic deformation at the crack tip becomes harder. The ductile-brittle transition is especially important in certain body-centered cubic metals and depends on loading rate and microstructure.

Brittle-material strength often shows statistical size effects because a larger volume has more opportunities to contain a severe flaw. Weibull models describe this variability, meaning one deterministic strength number can hide important reliability information.

White dwarfs are supported mainly by electron degeneracy pressure rather than ordinary thermal gas pressure. Because degeneracy pressure comes from quantum statistics, it does not simply vanish as the star cools.

The Master Theorem quickly classifies many divide-and-conquer recurrences, but only those with a particular regular form. Recurrences with uneven subproblem sizes, irregular additive terms, or changing branching factors can require other methods.

Reactive power does not represent net energy consumed over a full AC cycle, yet it affects current and voltage profiles in a power network. Local reactive-power support can help regulate voltage and reduce unnecessary current flow.

Refraction and the liquid outer core create angular regions where direct P or S waves are absent. These seismic shadow zones are valuable evidence for Earth's layered interior, showing how missing signals can constrain hidden structure.

The Fermi surface is the boundary in momentum space between occupied and unoccupied single-particle states at zero temperature. Many low-temperature electronic properties of metals are controlled mainly by states near that surface rather than equally by every electron deep below it.

A glass lacks the long-range periodic order of a crystal even though its local atomic arrangement can remain highly structured. The absence of periodicity changes diffraction patterns and produces a glass transition rather than an ordinary crystal melting point.

Versioning data, configuration, and analysis steps makes changes traceable across experiments. Reproducing only the final model file is insufficient when the preprocessing or source data that produced it have changed.

Air forced over mountains expands and cools, often increasing condensation and precipitation on the windward side. Descending air on the leeward side warms and dries, producing a rain-shadow tendency whose strength depends on atmospheric flow and moisture.

The graph Laplacian combines degree and adjacency information into a matrix whose eigenvalues reveal connectivity and diffusion structure. The number of zero eigenvalues equals the number of connected components.

In PID control, proportional action responds to present error, integral action accumulates past error to remove steady offset, and derivative action reacts to trends and can add damping. Larger gains are not universally better, and derivative action is especially sensitive to measurement noise.

During El Niño, weakened or rearranged tropical Pacific trade winds reduce normal eastern-Pacific upwelling and allow warm surface water to spread eastward. The event is a coupled ocean-atmosphere reorganization, not merely an isolated patch of warm ocean.

Mixing time measures how quickly a Markov chain forgets its starting state and approaches stationarity. A chain can possess a unique stationary distribution yet mix extremely slowly because bottlenecks impede movement between regions of state space.

Le Chatelier's principle is a qualitative guide to how equilibrium shifts after a disturbance, not a kinetic law that predicts the rate of change. A catalyst can speed both forward and reverse approaches to equilibrium without changing the equilibrium constant at fixed temperature.

Two dissimilar metals electrically connected in an electrolyte can form a galvanic couple, accelerating dissolution of the more active member. Severity also depends on area ratio, electrolyte resistance, and polarization, so standard electrode potentials alone do not fully predict engineering corrosion.

Evenly distributing request counts does not guarantee evenly distributed work if requests have different costs. Good load balancing may need estimates of queue length, service time, cache locality, or resource type rather than simple round-robin assignment.

Stars and gas in many galaxies orbit faster at large radii than the visible matter alone would predict under standard gravity. Extended dark-matter halos are one successful explanation, though rotation curves are one part of a wider body of evidence.

A superfluid can support flow with extremely low dissipation under suitable conditions and exhibits collective quantum behavior such as quantized vortices. Zero viscosity in one response does not mean every disturbance moves without energy loss.

The Arrhenius relation explains why many reaction rate constants rise rapidly with temperature as barrier crossing becomes more probable. Complex reactions can involve multiple pathways or mechanism changes, so one Arrhenius line need not describe an entire temperature range.

The Brier score measures squared error between predicted probabilities and binary outcomes. Unlike simple accuracy, it rewards well-calibrated confidence and penalizes both wrong predictions and excessive certainty.

An analog-to-digital converter maps continuous amplitudes to finite levels, creating quantization error. More bits reduce step size, but total accuracy is also limited by sensor noise, reference stability, and nonlinearity, so nominal resolution is not identical to effective resolution.
